skill.name: image-edit
skill.description: Routes image edit requests to RunComfy models for batch edits, text rewrites, multi-reference composition, local edits, and mask-based inpainting.
skill.summary: Route image editing tasks to the best RunComfy model and prompt pattern.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, placeholder URLs, or documented setup text rather than hidden code execution. Confirmed risks are intentional RunComfy CLI execution, third-party cloud processing of prompts and image URLs, and a cross-repository install instruction that should be verified.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the RunComfy CLI version, document exact trusted commands, and pass user prompts through structured input rather than ad hoc shell quoting.
Add a clear consent warning before sending private images, masks, prompts, or reference URLs to RunComfy cloud APIs.
Make the install command match the audited source repository or explain why agentspace-so/runcomfy-skills is the trusted install source.
Keep token storage owner-only, prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in CI, and avoid logging token paths or token values.

content.user_title: Edit Images with RunComfy Model Routing
content.value_statement: Image editing requests often need different models for text, identity, masks, and batch work. This skill selects the right RunComfy route and gives model-specific edit guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests among Nano Banana Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, Flux Kontext Pro, and Z-Image Turbo Inpaint.
Supports batch edits for 1 to 20 public image URLs through Nano Banana Edit.
Guides identity preservation, background swaps, object removal, and localized image changes.
Supports multilingual in-image text rewrite and multi-reference composition through GPT Image 2 Edit.
Uses mask-based inpainting guidance with strength and control scale settings.
Invokes the local RunComfy CLI with model-specific input schemas and output directories.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a RunComfy login or token.
Sends prompts, image URLs, and mask URLs to RunComfy cloud services.
Chooses one model route per request and does not blend multiple routes.
Requires public HTTPS image URLs, and inpainting also requires a grayscale mask URL.

use_cases.title: Create Consistent Product Variants
use_cases.description: Batch edit product images while keeping aspect ratio, resolution, subject identity, and brand framing consistent.

use_cases.title: Localize Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Rewrite in-image headlines across languages while preserving the original photograph, layout, and brand mark.

use_cases.title: Repair or Replace Image Regions
use_cases.description: Use masks to remove distractions, replace backgrounds, or retouch selected regions with controlled strength.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner image edit with one source image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit the image at [image URL]. Keep the subject identity, pose, clothing, and framing unchanged. Replace only the background with [new background].

prompt_templates.title: Batch Product Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Consistent edits across several product images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit these product images: [image URLs]. Keep each product unchanged. Remove background clutter and use a clean light studio backdrop.

prompt_templates.title: Multilingual Poster Rewrite
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace visible text while preserving the design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit the poster at [image URL]. Keep the photo, layout, and logo unchanged. Replace only the headline with [translated headline] in [script name].

prompt_templates.title: Masked Region Replacement
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced inpainting with a source image and mask.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [image URL] using mask [mask URL]. Replace the masked region with [new content]. Preserve lighting, texture, perspective, and all unmasked areas.

output_examples.input: A designer asks to replace a product photo background while preserving the item shape and label.
output_examples.output: The skill selects a general edit route, prioritizes identity preservation, and returns edited image files in the requested output directory.

output_examples.input: A localization team asks to change an English poster headline to Japanese while keeping the layout intact.
output_examples.output: The skill selects GPT Image 2 Edit, keeps the visual layout stable, and replaces only the in-image headline text.

output_examples.input: A production artist provides an image and mask to remove overhead cables from a street scene.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpaint, uses a cleanup strength setting, and preserves surrounding rooflines and sky tone.

best_practices: Start prompts with what must stay unchanged, then describe the edit.
Use masks for precise object removal or region replacement.
Lock aspect ratio and resolution when editing a batch.
anti_patterns: Do not send private images or sensitive prompts without approval.
Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not use low quality masks for precise inpainting work.

faq.question: Does this skill edit images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to send requests to RunComfy cloud models.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: You need a RunComfy login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value for CI and container use.

faq.question: Can it edit multiple images at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Nano Banana Edit supports batch edits with 1 to 20 input image URLs.

faq.question: Can it rewrite text inside an image?
faq.answer: Yes. The GPT Image 2 Edit route is intended for multilingual in-image text changes.

faq.question: When should I use a mask?
faq.answer: Use a grayscale mask when the edit must affect only a specific object or region.

faq.question: What happens to uploaded image URLs?
faq.answer: RunComfy model servers fetch the image and mask URLs needed to perform the requested edit.
